sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della guerra in corso tra Israele e Iran, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sceso a 18.02, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15, indicando una certa incertezza. Il DXY è salito a 98.14, mentre l'euro/dollaro è sceso a 1.17. I rendimenti dei bond USA a 10 anni sono scesi al 4.25%.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the ongoing war between Israel and Iran, negatively impacting equity markets and increasing demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX decreased to 18.02 but remains above 15, indicating some uncertainty. The DXY rose to 98.14, while the euro/dollar fell to 1.17. US 10-year bond yields decreased to 4.25%.

market_impact_summary.en: The Israel-Iran war continues to weigh on markets. Brent rose to $94.87, while gold rose to $4831.30/oz. Cryptos are weak, with Bitcoin at $73,895 and Ethereum at $2,320. Equity markets are weak, with S&P 500 at 6967.38 and STOXX 600 at 61.60.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con risultati positivi. Il Nikkei ha guadagnato lo 0,4% a 58.134 punti, mentre lo Shanghai ha registrato un aumento dello 0% a 4.000 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0,4% a 25.967 punti. Questi risultati potrebbero influenzare positivamente l'apertura dei mercati europei.

La giornata di oggi si apre con un sentiment di risk-off. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso con un guadagno dell'1,2% a 7.000 punti nella seduta precedente. Il Dollar Index (DXY) è stabile a 98 punti. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, scende dell'1,9% a 18 punti. I tassi di interesse continuano ad essere sotto attenzione: il tasso decennale USA scende dello 0,9% al 4,2%. L'oro, bene rifugio, guadagna lo 0,1% a 4.800 dollari l'oncia.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la situazione in Medio Oriente resta tesa. L'Iran ha minacciato di rallentare la crescita globale in caso di escalation del conflitto, secondo quanto avverte il Fondo Monetario Internazionale. Le esportazioni cinesi hanno subito un rallentamento a causa della turbolenza nella regione.

In ambito macroeconomico, gli occhi sono puntati sui dati del PIL degli Usa, in uscita il 29 aprile. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati, con un tasso di deposito al 2%. L'inflazione nell'Eurozona è attesa per il 2 aprile. Negli Usa, l'attenzione sarà sul fronte dei tassi di interesse, con la Fed che ha mantenuto il tasso tra il 3,5% e il 3,8%.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. La recente performance di prezzo ha visto BTC scendere a 73.800 dollari, con una variazione giornaliera del -0.9%. Sul fronte degli ETF, registriamo un afflusso netto giornaliero di 146 milioni di dollari, segno di un interesse ancora sostenuto per l'asset.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum è scesa a 2.300 dollari con un calo del 2.5%, mentre Solana ha toccato gli 83 dollari, in ribasso del 3.4%. Binance Coin (BNB) si trova a 610 dollari, con una diminuzione dello 0.8%.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment, l'indice Fear & Greed è a 23, in territorio di Extreme Fear. Questo indice misura la psicologia del mercato, e un valore basso come questo potrebbe indicare una maggiore avversione al rischio tra gli investitori.

In generale, il mercato crypto sembra essere influenzato dalle dinamiche macroeconomiche e dalle notizie regolamentari. Tra le notizie più recenti, segnaliamo una truffa elaborata che ha preso di mira gli utenti crypto tramite un'app di note molto popolare, e l'approvazione di un nuovo strumento di investimento legato a Bitcoin che ha raggiunto 2.7 miliardi di dollari in 48 ore.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global markets are experiencing a risk-off sentiment today, with investors becoming increasingly cautious amid rising geopolitical tensions. The VIX index is slightly lower, but still hovering around 18, indicating a sense of unease in the markets.

In traditional markets, equities are seeing a mixed performance. The S&P 500 is up 1.2% at 7000, while the STOXX 600 is flat at 62. The Nikkei and Hang Seng indices in Asia ended the session slightly higher, with gains of 0.4%. In the currency markets, the EUR/USD pair is up 0.2% at 1.2, while the Dollar Index (DXY) is flat at 98. Commodities are seeing modest gains, with gold up 0.1% at $4800/oz and Brent crude oil up 0.1% at $95. Bond yields are lower, with the US 10-year yield down 0.9% at 4.2% and the TLT Bond USA 20Y up 0.5% at 87.

On the macro front, investors are closely watching the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, with concerns that a wider conflict could impact global growth. The IMF has warned that a war in Iran could slow global growth to its weakest since the pandemic. In the US, the focus is on the upcoming earnings season, while in Europe, investors are awaiting the release of key economic data, including the Eurozone's GDP growth rate and inflation figures.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 

The Bitcoin ETF daily net inflow has been positive, with $146 million flowing in recently. This comes as BTC trades at $73,872, down 0.9% from its previous value. 

In our BTC deep dive, we note that despite the recent price action, the overall sentiment around Bitcoin remains cautiously optimistic. The recent inflows into BTC ETFs suggest that institutional investors continue to see value in the asset. 

Moving on to altcoins, we see a mixed bag of performances. ETH is down 2.5% at $2,320, while SOL and BNB are down 3.4% and 0.8% respectively, at $83 and $612. The altcoin market continues to be highly correlated with BTC's price action, but we're seeing some interesting developments in the space. For instance, Paxos Labs is looking to expand its offerings in yield, lending, and issuance tools, which could have a positive impact on the market.

In terms of sentiment and fear/greed, the Fear & Greed Index is currently at 23, indicating extreme fear. This could be a contrarian indicator, suggesting that we're near a local bottom. However, it's essential to keep in mind that the crypto market can be highly unpredictable and subject to sudden changes. As Iran conflict hints at Bitcoin's addressable market could exceed gold, according to Bitwise, we may see increased interest in safe-haven assets like BTC.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with more market insights. Keep an eye on the key events and data releases that could impact your trades. Until then, stay informed and stay ahead. A final word from Prais Alért - see you tomorrow. Have a great day!

articles.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
articles.snippet: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in an unstable ceasefire, has exposed a structural failure in the global semiconductor memory supply chain, and it is not the one analysts seem to be tracking. The story receiving attention is helium: Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility went offline, a 45-day inventory clock started running, and spot prices doubled within days. articles.title: Hungary Turns a New Page
articles.snippet: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán conceded defeat in a parliamentary election on April 12, ending his 16 years in power, after his Fidesz party lost its majority in parliament. The center-right Tisza party, led by Péter Magyar, won and is projected to have a two-thirds supermajority. Orbán has been a prominent right-wing populist, with close ties to the Trump administration in Washington and warm relations with Moscow. Magyar campaigned on promises to address corruption, improve the economy, and align more closely with Europe.We asked five experts to assess how the election results will shape Hungary’s role in Europe and its relationships The post Hungary Turns a New Page appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.snippet: The message given by Ursula von der Leyen to electrify the European economy is strategically coherent, politically appealing, and, on the surface, even unavoidable. articles.title: China’s Petrochemical Sector Cuts Output as Costs Climb
articles.snippet: Chinese petrochemical makers have started idling capacity as the cost of their feedstocks rises amid the Middle East war, Bloomberg has reported, noting that output is down to the lowest in three years. About a fifth of the country’s petrochemicals capacity has been taken offline, the publication wrote today, citing data from a Chinese industrial news outlet.
